The team

nT-Tao brings together a multidisciplinary team of physicists, engineers, and operators working on one of the most challenging engineering tasks of our time: commercializing compact, deployable fusion energy.

​​

We are expanding the team with people who want real ownership, deep technical responsibility, and the chance to help shape a new class of energy infrastructure.

Leadership

CEO, CO-FOUNDER
Oded Gour-Lavie

A retired Rear Admiral from the Israeli Navy, former commander of the Israeli Submarine Fleet, and the Israeli Sea Division. Culminating as Head of Legal & Strategic Policy in the IDF Planning Directorate. Oded is an Electrical Engineer with a BSc Cum Laude from Technion Haifa, Harvard-HKS Wexner Fellow (2008) and MIT Sloan-VF (2019).

CHIEF SCIENTIST, CO-FOUNDER
Doron Weinfeld

An accomplished physicist with 30 years of extensive experience in startups.

Doron is renowned for his technical creativity, out-of-the-box thinking, problem-solving ability, and theoretical expertise.

Doron has been engaged in plasma physics research for over 30 years.

CTO, CO-FOUNDER
Boaz Weinfeld

Boaz has an extensive background as an experimental physicist and system engineer across various fields, combined with a highly hands-on approach.

He brings over 18 years of experience in managerial and technology development roles at Intel, both in Israel and California.

Why National Water Infrastructure Is Becoming Power-Limited

National water infrastructure is inherently power-intensive. Treatment plants, desalination facilities, and pumping systems depend on continuous, reliable electricity to meet regulatory and public-health requirements. As grid reliability and long-term energy predictability become less certain, power availability is emerging as a defining constraint on water system resilience and expansion.

What Is Distributed Baseload Power?

For decades, electricity systems have been built around a simple assumption: power is generated in large, centralized facilities and delivered to users through extensive transmission and distribution networks.
